note: Structural assertions, graded by an independent reader against the run's visible output and the files it wrote. Baseline arm is the same prompt with the skill unavailable.

cases.prompt: /better-loop monitor the progression of all the benchmark runs, resolve harness or config errors, and restart the benchmarks as needed
assert: Chooses Monitor as the wake signal and says why polling is the wrong mechanism here
The proposed Monitor filter matches failure signatures as well as progress
Arms a heartbeat wakeup in the 1200-1800s range and explains it is the backstop, not the signal
Writes .claude/loop.md and reports its byte size against the 25,000 cap
Arms a day-six renewal reminder and names the expiry date
Reports the job ID

cases.prompt: /better-loop keep implementing until you have verified the feature is 100% complete
assert: Identifies this as a finish line rather than a cadence
Routes to better-goal instead of arming a loop
Does not arm a loop that would tick past completion

cases.prompt: what exactly is performing the loop? I expected to see a monitor or a script running
assert: Explains that a dynamic loop is a scheduled wakeup with no visible process
Distinguishes 'invisible' from 'not running' rather than treating the loop as broken
Checks the actual scheduled tasks rather than guessing
Offers the Monitor as the visible wake signal

cases.prompt: /better-loop 7m check the deploy and fix anything broken
assert: Flags that 7m does not divide 60 and states what it rounds to
Mentions the jitter window rather than implying exact timing
Includes a stop condition so it does not run to the seven-day expiry

cases.prompt: /better-loop run /verify on the branch every 30 minutes
assert: Flags that /verify is disable-model-invocation and arrives at a fire as plain text
Proposes the underlying command or a main-turn invocation instead
Does not arm a loop that would tick correctly and verify nothing

cases.prompt: /better-loop watch CI and address review comments (session will be resumed tomorrow)
assert: States that Monitor and background Bash tasks are never restored on resume
Puts a re-arm step at the top of the tick protocol
Notes that recurring crons within 7 days do survive resume, so the two behave differently

process_evals: The mechanism is chosen and justified before any file is written
The loop.md byte size is stated, not estimated
The final report names: mechanism, job ID, cadence, wake signal, expiry date, ledger path, stop instructions
Nothing is armed when preflight blocks
The skill does not begin doing the underlying work in the arming pass
